newsitem.title: USA: Emerging market debt up, Russia Vnesh sets record.
newsitem.headline: Emerging market debt up, Russia Vnesh sets record.

text.p: Aided by the upturn in U.S. Treasuries, emerging market debts extended the winning streak to end the week on a high note.
Russia's dollar Vnesh loan trading made another record high as diminishing deal risk drew more investors into the market, traders said.
Overall, the abundant liquidity that buoyed the emerging market bonds showed no signs of drying up and all recent new supplies were smoothly absorbed, they said.
The market maintained a firm tone, even early when the U.S. bonds tumbled on the U.S. payroll data for May.
The data sent ambiguous signals about the strength of the labor market. Emerging market debts made more gains when U.S. Treasuries flipped higher, traders said.

The U.S. Labor Department reported that non-farm payrolls rose by 138,000 last month, but the April increase was revised to a whopping 323,000 from 142,000. The unemployment rate at 4.8 percent was the lowest level in more than 23 years.

While prospects the Federal Reserve might tighten credit in July kept investors edgy, fund managers could not afford to sit on the sidelines half-way through the year, said Kip Allardt, emerging market debt strategist at CS First Boston.
"As long as we have a benign U.S. market, I think we can go higher," he said.

The widely watched sovereign spread of the J.P. Morgan Emerging Markets Brady Index tightened about another 3 points to 405 on Friday, the narrowest level in 1997 and closing in on the all-time record of 392 set on January 7, 1994.

Recent market turmoil in Thailand and the Czech Republic had made Latin American assets appear relatively safe, Allardt said. Meanwhile, Russia convinced even the most reluctant investors that its assets were attractive as the loan reconciliations progressed on schedule, he said.
Russia dollar Vnesh made a fresh record high at 89-5/8. In late afternoon trading, it was bid 89-1/2, up 1-1/4 on the day.
Latin Par bonds gained with the Treasuries rally, adding about one point. The Eurobond sectors also did well.

The freshly minted Brazil Global 27 jumped 1.00 to 96-3/4 bid. Argentina GLB-17 rose 1-1/8 to 110-5/8 bid, and Mexico UMS 26 added 7/8 to 112-1/4 bid. Venezuela bonds took a pause after Thursday's rally on the sovereign credit upgrade. Standard & Poor's raised the country's long-term foreign currency rating to single B lus from single B.
Rafael de la Fuente, analyst at Paribas Securities, said Venezuela Bradys were now "close to fair value," as the upgrade by S&P was overdue.
He pointed out that the Moody's had maintained a Ba2 rating, which was equivalent of a double-B standing on S&P's rating scheme.
The offering of a $315 million 10-year eurobond, along with credit upgrade, would pave the way for a Brady exchange in a larger global bond offer, de la Fuente said.
Veneauela FLIRB was unchanged at 92.00 bid.
